subject: Capacity reconciliation & commit-topup agreement for ClearSight Labs
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex@clearsight.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected July overage + request to expand capacity

Marissa,

Hope you're well. We ran into a sizable unexpected usage spike in July — attached is a CSV export of token-hours and job counts for the month. Our engineers underestimated a new batch job and we ended up consuming ~2.1x our committed capacity.

We want to: 1) reconcile the overage (one-off invoice or credit), and 2) look at adding committed capacity starting Sept 1 to avoid repeat incidents. We're open to a blended settlement + purchase of additional capacity.

Can you advise next steps and what you need from our side? Procurement may require an amended SOW / PO.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering, ClearSight Labs
procurement@clearsight.com

Attachment: CS_usage_report_Jul2026.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@clearsight.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected July overage + request to expand capacity

Alex — thanks for the export, that helped. Quick summary from our side after an initial pass: total billable tokens for July are ~2.05x the committed baseline, which maps to an overage of ~4,300 token-hours.

Proposed path to close this quickly:
- One-time reconciliation invoice for the July overage (we can issue an invoice or apply a credit against future spend).
- Apply a one-off partial credit equal to 25% of the overage charge as a gesture to preserve the relationship while you migrate critical batch jobs into a burst/queue pattern.
- Start a committed-topup effective 2026-09-01 for an additional 30% capacity with a 12-month addendum to your existing term (we'll draft the amendment).

If that sounds reasonable, Neha (cc'd) will prepare a short amendment and Ben can scope the final credit/invoice split with finance. To move procurement along, can you have your PO contact confirm billing address and a PO number (even a placeholder) so we can draft the amendment for signature?

I attached a working amendment draft with the capacity numbers filled in to speed review.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachment: proposed-amendment-DEAL-78321.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected July overage + request to expand capacity

Ben / Neha — looping you in. Alex sent us the usage export. My recommendation (see draft): carve out a one-off reconciliation invoice for the raw overage, then apply a 25% credit to soften the impact. We push the customer to take the 30% committed-topup for 12 months (adds predictable MRR).

Two operational asks:
1) Ben — can you confirm the financial math and whether Finance is ok to book a 25% promotional credit against the overage (we should show it as a contra-charge on the invoice)? Also confirm whether we need an SOW amendment ID or if the amendment PDF is sufficient (I prefer amendment + PO).
2) Neha — once Ben confirms, can you own the customer coordination and get a PO (procurement) or an explicit email acceptance from Alex? If procurement needs net-60 terms, flag that early.

Quoting Alex below for context.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Finance Billing <billing@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected July overage + request to expand capacity

Team — ran numbers with Finance. Confirmation:
- Gross overage amount (pre-credit): $28,640
- 25% goodwill credit recommended: $7,160
- Net one-off invoice: $21,480
- Proposed committed-topup (30% uplift) adds $9,800/month; we'll pro-rate Sept based on contract calendar.

Finance confirmed they can issue a net-30 invoice to ClearSight for $21,480; if procurement requires net-60 we need explicit approval from Rev Ops (cc'ing billing). Ben attached a draft invoice stub in Drive.

Ben Carter
Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
Attachment stub: invoice-stub-DEAL-78321.pdf (placed in Drive link)
From: Alex Johnson <alex@clearsight.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity reconciliation & commit-topup agreement for ClearSight Labs

Marissa / Ben / Neha — thanks for moving quickly. Procurement is ok with the proposed approach. We've attached a PO (PO_78934.pdf) that references the amendment and asks for a net-30 invoice. PO contact: procurement@clearsight.com.

We accept the one-time net invoice of $21,480 and will sign the 12-month topup amendment effective 2026-09-01. Please issue the invoice and send the final amendment for signature; procurement will return a signed copy once the invoice is issued and the amendment is countersigned.

Appreciate the fair credit and the pragmatic topup path — should avoid surprises in Q4.

Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering, ClearSight Labs
Attachment: PO_78934.pdf
